I was 13 when Half-Life came out, but I got it the next year in '99 for my 14th birthday cause that's how shit worked back then, you had to wait for your birthday or Christmas if you wanted your parents to buy you anything.

It was the second game where I really got into the online community with the in game Half-Life chat, and then through that learning about gamespy and Planet Half-Life. I don't think there has ever been an online community like HL1 had. You had the SDK kit released by Valve super quick and the game shipped with the Worldcraft level editor which was more complicated then the Build engine that Duke Nukem 3D came with but it was still simple enough even for a 14 year old to use. I remember Radium was the absolute top quality site for maps with constant updates and a good forum. You had whole websites dedicated to prefabs that you could import into maps and it was pretty much total freedom for the mapping, modeling and modding community.

When Team Fortress Classic dropped I was in love. I was in a clan with some friends from high school and some guys in Sweden. I was lucky enough to have a DSL line so I pwned everyone in DM, TFC and then Counterstrike. Oh yes Counterstike came out pretty early in the early betas. I remember the first beta playing cs_assault and you could barely tell the difference between the terrorists and the counter terrorists cause the models and skins were so close. Plus I was still playing in software mode for the longest time. When I got a Voodoo 2 card that could do OpenGL my mind was blown and I was sure there was no way they could ever make video game graphics better then the smoothness of OpenGL.

Half-Life had the best singleplayer experience I can remember. It was so original even back then. From the opening sequence on the tram ride you got a feeling you were in a real huge underground secret complex. The other games before then like Quake and Quake 2 all had sci-fi type environments. Half-Life was the first to have realistic building like office complexes and laboratories. It made it so much easier to get lost in the game's story. Scripted sequences were almost never used in games and Half-Life threw them at you all over the place which really fleshed out the environment.

The atmosphere was the best in HL1 it reminds me of that exact time of my life, spending my whole summer vacation playing through the game and online every day. Its difficult to even really put it into words, a specific place at a specific time. I never got the atmosphere in HL2, it was a good game but it did not have the vibe of the original. It was such a great game for its time, they had to rethink how they did FPS games after Half-Life. It was really groundbreaking if you were already playing games at that time and then you came across Half-Life.

I can blaze through half life in a 6 hour sitting nowadays. The Black Mesa version in Steam is a very good update of the original game in the Source engine. Its good to hear the original HL1 still holds up in 2017 for new gamers who did not get to experience it at the time.
